GUIDANCE ANALYSIS: Deere & Company — Q2 2026

GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: $4.5 billion to $5.0 billion
UNIT: USD billions
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: GAAP net income attributable to Deere & Company; outlook maintained
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Diversified portfolio and segment performance support a stable enterprise outlook amid agricultural-market volatility.
- Small Agriculture & Turf and Construction & Forestry strength offsets pressures in large agriculture.

UNIT: %

COMPARABLE EARNINGS ANALYSIS: Deere & Company — Q3 2026
STRICT REPORT WINDOW: 2026-07-06 to 2026-08-16

COMPARABLE: AGCO Corporation (AGCO)
REPORT DATE: 2026-07-30
REPORTED PERIOD: Second quarter ended June 30, 2026
WHY COMPARABLE: AGCO is a global agricultural-machinery and precision-agriculture OEM with direct overlap in tractors, combines, hay equipment and farm technology. Its release provides direct evidence on farmer capital-equipment demand, dealer/production alignment, crop-economics pressure and tariff costs.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- Farmer income, crop economics and agricultural input-cost uncertainty
- North American tractor and combine retail demand
- Latin American farm-equipment demand
- Tariffs and equipment-manufacturing input costs
- Dealer inventory and production alignment
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Cautious equipment purchasing amid rising uncertainty around farm input costs and demand, uneven crop economics and macroeconomic uncertainty [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: AGCO said farmers delayed equipment investments and that net sales fell 3.7% year over year on a constant-currency basis. It reduced its 2026 sales outlook to $10.1-$10.2 billion and said production would be aligned with dealer inventory and market demand.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Directionally negative for Deere agricultural-equipment demand and production absorption, particularly where farmer cash economics and financing conditions delay purchases. The release does not support transferring AGCO's sales percentage directly to Deere because product, geographic and channel mix differ.
  SOURCE: https://investors.agcocorp.com/news-releases/news-release-details/agco-reports-second-quarter-results-18
- North American and Latin American agricultural-equipment demand [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: AGCO reported North American industry retail sales for the first six months of 2026 down 9% for tractors and 7% for combines. In Latin America, second-quarter constant-currency sales fell 25.0% as softer industry demand reduced sales across product categories; regional operating income was $48.7 million lower, primarily from lower sales and production volumes.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The North American tractor/combine data are a direct cautionary signal for Deere's agricultural-equipment demand. The Latin American weakness also indicates risk to farm-equipment volume and factory utilization, but the magnitude cannot be assumed for Deere given differing regional mix and dealer inventories.
  SOURCE: https://investors.agcocorp.com/news-releases/news-release-details/agco-reports-second-quarter-results-18
- Tariff-related manufacturing costs, partly offset by tariff refunds [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: AGCO stated that North American operating results were approximately flat year over year primarily because higher tariff-related costs were partly offset by approximately $22 million of certain IEEPA tariff refunds recognized during the quarter.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The evidence indicates a margin headwind from tariffs for agricultural-equipment manufacturers, with the realized effect dependent on sourcing, mitigation and refund eligibility. It is not a basis to assign Deere the same dollar refund or cost exposure.
  SOURCE: https://investors.agcocorp.com/news-releases/news-release-details/agco-reports-second-quarter-results-18
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://investors.agcocorp.com/news-releases/news-release-details/agco-reports-second-quarter-results-18

COMPARABLE: CNH Industrial N.V. (CNH)
REPORT DATE: 2026-08-03
REPORTED PERIOD: Second quarter ended June 30, 2026
WHY COMPARABLE: CNH is a direct global agricultural-equipment OEM competitor through Case IH and New Holland Agriculture, with overlapping tractors, combines, precision agriculture, dealer channels and farmer end markets.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- North American, EMEA and South American tractor/combine demand
- Farmer commodity-price and input-cost economics
- Pricing versus volume trade-off
- Tariffs, transportation costs and labor inflation
- Dealer inventory reduction and low production levels
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Weak tractor and combine industry volumes across core agricultural regions [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: CNH reported second-quarter North American industry volume down 16% for tractors under 140 HP, down 17% for tractors over 140 HP and down 7% for combines. It also reported EMEA tractor and combine demand down 11% and 1%, respectively, and South American tractor and combine demand down 8% and 29%.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This is a direct negative demand read-through for Deere's agricultural-equipment businesses, especially large tractors and combines in North America. Deere's shipment result may differ because of its higher-horsepower mix, order coverage, production cadence and regional exposure.
  SOURCE: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/03/3337315/0/en/cnh-industrial-n-v-reports-second-quarter-2026-results.html
- Price realization offsetting lower agricultural volumes, while mix and tariffs pressured profitability [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: CNH Agriculture net sales were $3.277 billion, down 1% at constant currency, as favorable price realization offset lower South American volume. Adjusted EBIT declined $93 million to $170 million and margin fell 290 basis points to 5.2%, primarily due to lower South American volumes, unfavorable North American and EMEA mix, tariffs, higher labor-driven SG&A and higher R&D expense.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The result supports a mixed Deere read-through: pricing can cushion revenue against lower unit demand, but unfavorable volume/mix and tariff costs can compress agricultural operating profit. The 290-basis-point margin movement is not transferable to Deere because CNH's pricing, cost structure and regional mix are different.
  SOURCE: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/03/3337315/0/en/cnh-industrial-n-v-reports-second-quarter-2026-results.html
- Low commodity prices, high farm input costs and uncertain trade policy [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: CNH characterized 2026 as a trough year for the agricultural cycle, citing low commodity prices, high input costs and an uncertain trade environment. It said it was maintaining low production levels and working with dealers to reduce channel inventory; its Agriculture outlook was for approximately flat 2026 sales and a 5.0%-5.5% adjusted EBIT margin.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This is a negative directional indicator for Deere's farmer-investment environment and production absorption. It does not establish the size or timing of Deere's Q3 effect.
  SOURCE: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/03/3337315/0/en/cnh-industrial-n-v-reports-second-quarter-2026-results.html
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/03/3337315/0/en/cnh-industrial-n-v-reports-second-quarter-2026-results.html

COMPARABLE: Kubota Corporation (KUBTY)
REPORT DATE: 2026-08-04
REPORTED PERIOD: Six months ended June 30, 2026
WHY COMPARABLE: Kubota is a publicly traded global farm-equipment manufacturer with direct overlap in tractors and agricultural machinery. Its disclosed market commentary is relevant to farm-income conditions and agricultural demand in North America, Europe and Asia, although its reported Farm & Industrial Machinery segment also includes engines and construction machinery.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- North American farmer-income conditions and tractor demand
- European agricultural-product prices and tractor-market conditions
- Asian farm-income conditions
- Agricultural-equipment pricing
- Tariffs and inflation-related input costs
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Deteriorating farmer-income conditions and weak agricultural-product prices [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Kubota said North American agricultural demand slowed as farmers' income conditions worsened; European tractor demand remained sluggish amid depressed agricultural-product prices; and Thailand's market remained weak against weak farm incomes. These conditions occurred within a Farm & Industrial Machinery segment whose six-month revenue increased 18.1%, but the company did not quantify the agricultural-only revenue effect.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: Directionally negative for Deere farm-equipment demand in the affected regions. Because Kubota combines farm equipment with construction machinery and engines in the reported segment, its reported segment growth cannot be treated as an agricultural-only demand signal for Deere.
  SOURCE: https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/137q2e.pdf
- Price revisions and North American volume growth, offset in part by tariff and inflation costs [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Kubota reported Farm & Industrial Machinery operating profit up 56.4% to ¥212.2 billion, principally from price revisions, higher North American sales volumes, favorable exchange rates and U.S. tariff refunds, despite U.S.-tariff-related costs and inflation-driven expenses. The company did not separate the agricultural contribution from construction machinery and engines.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This supports the proposition that price and tariff-refund effects can partially offset cost pressure, but the segment aggregation prevents a defensible numerical transfer to Deere's Production & Precision Ag profit or consolidated EPS.
  SOURCE: https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/137q2e.pdf
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/137q2e.pdf

PRELIMINARY COMPARABLE-ONLY METRIC ADD-ONS:
- Worldwide net sales and revenues: 0 USDm (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: $0m = no transferable target-period dollar base × comparable demand signal. The qualifying releases provide a negative/mixed directional signal: AGCO reported 3.7% constant-currency sales decline and weaker industry retail demand; CNH Agriculture sales were down 1% at constant currency as pricing offset lower volume; Kubota's farm-equipment commentary was negative but its reported segment includes non-agricultural businesses. None of the qualifying releases provides a Deere-specific worldwide-sales base, product/geographic weighting, or shipment timing factor that can be used without importing non-qualifying target-company evidence. Therefore the defensible comparable-only transfer coefficient is 0.
  ASSUMPTION: Only AGCO, CNH and Kubota releases dated July 30, August 3 and August 4, 2026 are used.
  ASSUMPTION: No percentage change from a comparable is assumed to recur at Deere.
  ASSUMPTION: No Deere sales base, dealer-inventory position, product mix, production schedule or target-company information is used.
  ASSUMPTION: Zero is an evidence-discipline outcome, not a conclusion that the peer demand signal is neutral.
  SOURCE: https://investors.agcocorp.com/news-releases/news-release-details/agco-reports-second-quarter-results-18
  SOURCE: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/03/3337315/0/en/cnh-industrial-n-v-reports-second-quarter-2026-results.html
  SOURCE: https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/137q2e.pdf
- Diluted EPS (GAAP): 0 USD / share (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: $0.00/share = no defensible conversion of comparable operating effects into Deere GAAP net income per diluted share. AGCO's reported EPS includes material non-comparable items, CNH's cited segment measure is adjusted EBIT, and Kubota reports IFRS and did not report diluted EPS. The qualifying releases do not supply a Deere tax rate, interest/financial-services effect, non-operating items or diluted-share count; therefore the comparable-only EPS transfer coefficient is 0.
  ASSUMPTION: Only macro and industry effects are retained; peer-specific financing, divestiture, tax and accounting effects are excluded.
  ASSUMPTION: No conversion of CNH adjusted EBIT, AGCO reported EPS or Kubota IFRS profit into Deere GAAP EPS is assumed.
  ASSUMPTION: No Deere diluted-share count, tax rate, financing result or non-operating items are used.
  SOURCE: https://investors.agcocorp.com/news-releases/news-release-details/agco-reports-second-quarter-results-18
  SOURCE: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/03/3337315/0/en/cnh-industrial-n-v-reports-second-quarter-2026-results.html
  SOURCE: https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/137q2e.pdf
- Production & Precision Ag operating profit: 0 USDm (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: $0m = no transferable Deere Production & Precision Ag revenue base × no defensible peer-to-Deere margin conversion. CNH's direct Agriculture comparable showed adjusted EBIT down $93m and margin down 290 basis points, with volume, mix, tariff and labor-cost pressure. AGCO also cited lower Latin American sales/production volumes and tariff costs. However, neither release discloses an exposure-equivalent Deere segment base, pricing realization, tariff sourcing profile, manufacturing absorption or mix. Kubota's segment is additionally blended with construction machinery and engines. The defensible comparable-only scaling factor is consequently 0.
  ASSUMPTION: CNH's adjusted EBIT is treated as directional industry evidence only, not as a GAAP operating-profit proxy for Deere.
  ASSUMPTION: AGCO's tariff refund and Kubota's tariff-refund, foreign-exchange and construction-equipment effects are not transferred.
  ASSUMPTION: No Deere Production & Precision Ag sales base, operating margin, tax, product mix, regional mix or factory-utilization data are used.
  ASSUMPTION: The underlying read-through is negative/mixed, but no absolute USDm add-on is defensible under the stated evidence restriction.
  SOURCE: https://investors.agcocorp.com/news-releases/news-release-details/agco-reports-second-quarter-results-18
  SOURCE: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/03/3337315/0/en/cnh-industrial-n-v-reports-second-quarter-2026-results.html
  SOURCE: https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/137q2e.pdf

events.title: U.S. tariff reduction for specified agricultural and mobile industrial equipment
events.summary: President Trump reduced the tariff rate on specified agricultural equipment, including combines and harvesters, to 15% from 25%. The order also applied a 15% rate to certain imported mobile industrial equipment, including bulldozers and forklifts, from countries with U.S. trade deals.
source_headlines: Trump lowers tariffs on farming equipment, adjusts steel and aluminum imports

events.title: May 2026 U.S. agricultural tractor and combine retail-sales decline
events.summary: AEM reported that U.S. agricultural-tractor retail sales declined 21.6% year over year in May 2026, while U.S. combine sales declined 56.1%. AEM characterized the results as continued market softness amid farmer economic pressure, depressed commodity prices, and uncertainty around trade and farm policy.
source_headlines: Agricultural Tractor and Combine Sales See Declines Across the U.S. and Canada in May 2026

events.title: FTC and five-state right-to-repair settlement with Deere
events.summary: The FTC and five states settled their antitrust lawsuit against Deere through a stipulated order. Deere must provide farmers and independent repair providers repair resources equivalent to those available to authorized dealers, including specified software capabilities. Similar future resources must be made available once they are provided to more than half of Deere's U.S. authorized dealer network. The order runs for 10 years and may be extended for violations. The source did not quantify a financial effect.
source_headlines: FTC, States Secure Settlement with Deere & Company, Advancing Farmers’ Right to Repair

events.title: Deere Funding Canada Corporation issuance of 4.850% notes due 2031
events.summary: Deere Funding Canada Corporation, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Deere, agreed to sell $300 million aggregate principal amount of 4.850% notes due July 15, 2031. The notes were scheduled to settle on July 15, 2026, are fully and unconditionally guaranteed by Deere & Company, and pay interest semiannually beginning January 15, 2027.
source_headlines: Deere Funding Canada Corporation 4.850% Notes due 2031

events.title: June 2026 U.S. agricultural tractor decline and combine-sales increase
events.summary: AEM reported that U.S. combine retail sales increased 3.9% year over year in June 2026, while total U.S. agricultural-tractor sales declined 18.4%. Through June 2026, U.S. total tractor sales were down 13.6% and combine sales were down 11.4% from the comparable 2025 period.
source_headlines: U.S. and Canadian Sales of Combines See Slight Increase in June 2026

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Q3 FY2026 forecast = $12,356m; projected change = $12,356m - prior reported Q2 FY2026 actual of $13,369m = -$1,013m. GUIDANCE bridge: FY2025 worldwide net sales and revenues of $45,684m x 1.055 central interpretation of management's '>5%' FY2026 growth outlook = $48,197m FY2026. Less reported FY2026 H1 revenue of $22,981m = implied H2 revenue of $25,216m. Management said back-half revenue would be slightly higher than H1 and Q4 would exceed Q3; therefore Q3 is set at 49.0% of H2: $25,216m x 49.0% = $12,356m, with $12,860m implied for Q4.

event_contributions.affected_line: sales volume, price realization, currency translation, and mix
event_contributions.transmission_path: FY segment shipment-volume outlook plus price and currency assumptions -> consolidated equipment net sales; Financial Services and other revenues continue within the company-wide top-line outlook -> Worldwide net sales and revenues.
assumptions: Management's stated 'grow by more than 5%' company top-line guidance is converted to a 5.5% central case, not a mechanically exact company forecast.
FY2025 worldwide net sales and revenues were $45,684m.
Q3 receives 49.0% of implied H2 revenue because management specifically indicated Q4 revenue would exceed Q3; this is a modestly back-end-weighted allocation rather than an equal split.
The May 21 guidance already contemplated subdued PPA demand, strong SAT and Construction & Forestry growth, pricing, currency, and tariff-related demand effects.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. FY2026 revenue = FY2025 $45,684m x (1 + 5.5%) = $48,197m. Implied H2 = $48,197m - reported H1 $22,981m = $25,216m. Q3 = $25,216m x 49.0% = $12,356m. Change versus prior reported Q2 = $12,356m - $13,369m = -$1,013m.

event_contributions.affected_line: production cost / tariff cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: Lower tariff rate on specified imported agricultural and mobile-industrial equipment could lower COGS and potentially affect customer pricing; it does not create a quantified Q3 shipment or recognized-revenue change for Deere.
assumptions: Deere's May guidance already incorporated a $900m net direct-tariff-cost outlook and described direct tariff exposure as broadly unchanged after policy changes.
No Deere-specific import value, product eligibility, customer-price response, or Q3 shipment timing was disclosed for the June 2 action.
No sales effect is recognized without a defensible Deere-specific volume or pricing coefficient.
event_contributions.calculation: MIXED ROUTE. Potential tariff-cost relief would primarily affect COGS, not revenue. Because no eligible Deere revenue realization is quantified and the guidance narrative already contemplated evolving tariff policy, incremental Q3 worldwide-sales contribution = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: retail demand / dealer inventory / future shipment volume
event_contributions.transmission_path: Weak May tractor and combine retail activity -> potential dealer restocking reduction and lower PPA shipments -> lower PPA sales and consolidated worldwide revenue.
assumptions: The May retail data arrived after guidance but are retail registrations rather than Deere shipments or Deere-specific retail sales.
Management's FY guidance had already assumed U.S. and Canada large-ag industry unit sales down 15%-20%, subdued PPA shipments, and cautious agricultural demand.
The June data in E5 partly reverses the extreme monthly combine signal and provides the more complete available May-June read-through.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED READ-THROUGH. May U.S. retail tractors were down 21.6% and combines down 56.1%, but no defensible dealer-to-Deere shipment conversion or Q3 timing factor is disclosed. The signal changes the risk narrative a little but not the guidance-based central revenue estimate: $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: operating expense, legal expense, service-parts/service revenue mix
event_contributions.transmission_path: Right-to-repair settlement requirements could create implementation and compliance expense and could alter longer-run dealer-service economics; no quantified Q3 revenue recognition effect was disclosed.
assumptions: The settlement specifies repair-resource access and reporting obligations over a 10-year term but no payment, accrued charge, implementation budget, or Q3 accounting-recognition amount.
Deere's May 3 filing had already disclosed the FTC matter and stated that its business impact could not then be estimated.
No revenue effect is inferred from a regulatory settlement without disclosed customer uptake, price, cost, or accounting information.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. There is no identified fine or quantified Q3 charge, and no identifiable Q3 sales effect. Incremental Q3 worldwide-sales contribution = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: interest expense / financing cash flow
event_contributions.transmission_path: New debt issuance -> interest expense, subject to use of proceeds and refinancing effects; it has no direct revenue transmission.
assumptions: The $300m notes settled July 15, 2026, but the filing does not establish whether proceeds incrementally increased debt versus refinancing or funding Financial Services.
The issuance has no direct effect on equipment shipment volume, selling price, or revenue recognition.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Financing affects interest expense rather than revenue; incremental Q3 worldwide-sales contribution = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: retail demand / dealer inventory / future shipment volume
event_contributions.transmission_path: June tractor decline and combine improvement -> dealer retail throughput and inventory absorption -> possible PPA shipment timing -> consolidated revenue.
assumptions: June U.S. tractors declined 18.4% year over year, but combines increased 3.9%; through June, tractors were down 13.6% and combines down 11.4%.
The year-to-date retail data are broadly consistent with management's already-guided 15%-20% U.S./Canada large-ag industry decline, especially after allowing for product-category mix.
No Deere-specific Q3 dealer orders, shipment schedule, or production change was disclosed.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED READ-THROUGH. June's combine recovery moderates E2's May downside signal. The available retail evidence changes the agricultural-demand narrative only a little and leaves the already-guided central Q3 revenue estimate unchanged: $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: agricultural-equipment demand, production absorption, pricing, tariffs, and mix
event_contributions.transmission_path: AGCO/CNH/Kubota agricultural commentary -> possible industry demand and margin read-through -> Deere PPA shipments and profit -> consolidated sales and earnings.
assumptions: AGCO and CNH indicate weak agricultural demand and production alignment, while Kubota's disclosed segment is materially mixed with construction machinery and engines.
The supplied comparable analysis found no defensible Deere-specific worldwide-revenue base, exposure weighting, shipment-timing factor, or peer-to-Deere conversion coefficient.
Comparable effects are not copied because Deere's PPA geographic mix, dealer inventory, pricing, currency, and production cadence differ.
event_contributions.calculation: Comparable-only incremental transfer = $0m. The peer releases reinforce the risks already present in Deere guidance and in the AEM data, but no independently scalable Q3 Deere revenue impact remains after avoiding double counting.

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Q3 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS forecast = $3.81; projected change = $3.81 - prior reported Q2 FY2026 diluted EPS of $6.55 = -$2.74 per share. FY net-income guidance midpoint is $4,750m. Less reported H1 net income attributable to Deere of $2,429m leaves $2,321m for H2. Q3 is allocated $1,030m, or 44.4% of implied H2 net income, reflecting management's statement that Q4 revenue is higher than Q3 and that Q4 has the most favorable cost comparisons.

event_contributions.affected_line: consolidated revenue, operating margin, interest expense, tax, and diluted share count
event_contributions.transmission_path: Q3 revenue and operating-margin phasing -> consolidated operating income -> pretax income after net non-operating expense -> GAAP net income at the 25% guided tax midpoint -> diluted EPS using a 270.5m share count.
assumptions: FY2026 net-income midpoint is $4,750m; management's 24%-26% effective-tax-rate range is represented by 25%.
Q3 revenue is the $12,356m guidance-phased worldwide-sales forecast.
Q3 consolidated operating margin is calibrated at 11.938% to reconcile the income-statement bridge to $1,030m GAAP net income attributable to Deere.
Net non-operating expense is $101.7m, consistent with Deere's reported consolidated reconciliation framework and excluding an unquantified refinancing effect.
Diluted shares are 270.5m, slightly below Q2's 270.8m due to completed repurchases; no incremental share buyback after May 3 is assumed beyond this modest central estimate.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. FY net income midpoint = ($4,500m + $5,000m) / 2 = $4,750m. Implied H2 net income = $4,750m - reported H1 $2,429m = $2,321m. Q3 net income allocation = $2,321m x 44.4% = $1,030m. EPS bridge: operating income = $12,356m x 11.938% = $1,475.0m; pretax income = $1,475.0m - $101.7m + $0m = $1,373.3m; net income = $1,373.3m x (1 - 25.0%) + $0m = $1,030.0m; diluted EPS = $1,030.0m / 270.5m = $3.81. Change = $3.81 - $6.55 = -$2.74.

event_contributions.affected_line: COGS / tariff cost / tax
event_contributions.transmission_path: Potential tariff-cost reduction -> lower COGS -> higher operating and pretax income -> tax -> EPS; no Deere-specific incremental tariff-cost amount or recognition timing is available.
assumptions: The May guidance already quantified direct tariff costs and described tariff exposure as essentially unchanged despite policy developments.
No eligible Deere import base or effective tariff-rate reduction is disclosed.
event_contributions.calculation: No defensible incremental pretax-income amount can be isolated from guidance; EPS effect = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: shipment volume / production absorption / COGS
event_contributions.transmission_path: May retail weakness could reduce Deere agricultural shipments and factory absorption -> PPA operating profit -> consolidated pretax income -> tax -> EPS.
assumptions: May registrations do not identify Deere-specific Q3 shipments, sales incentives, production changes, or factory-cost absorption.
The event is subsumed by the guided agricultural downturn and moderated by the June update.
event_contributions.calculation: No defensible incremental Deere pretax-income amount after guidance and E5 reconciliation; EPS effect = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: legal expense / implementation expense / service mix
event_contributions.transmission_path: Settlement compliance could increase operating expense or affect longer-run service economics -> pretax income -> tax -> EPS.
assumptions: No fine, implementation cost, reserve increase, or Q3 accounting recognition amount was disclosed.
The order's required actions extend over 10 years, so a full-period charge cannot be inferred.
event_contributions.calculation: Unquantified regulatory requirements cannot be converted to GAAP net income; EPS effect = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: interest expense
event_contributions.transmission_path: July 15 debt settlement -> possible incremental interest expense -> lower pretax income -> tax shield -> lower EPS.
assumptions: The issuance was $300m at 4.850%, but disclosed use of proceeds does not establish that debt rose on a net basis rather than refinancing existing funding.

Even if treated as wholly incremental, only roughly 18 days fall within Deere's Q3 ending August 2, implying approximately $0.7m pretax interest, roughly $0.002 per diluted share after tax, which rounds to $0.00.
The guidance-based bridge therefore retains its net-non-operating-expense assumption.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Illustrative maximum unhedged incremental Q3 interest = $300m x 4.850% x 18/365 = about $0.7m pretax; after 25% tax and 270.5m shares = about -$0.002/share. Because refinancing/use-of-proceeds offset is unknown, recognized incremental EPS effect is $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: shipment volume / production absorption / COGS
event_contributions.transmission_path: June agricultural retail results -> potential PPA shipments and factory utilization -> operating income -> net income -> EPS.
assumptions: June combines improved while tractors remained weak, and year-to-date trends remain consistent with Deere's guided large-ag downturn.
No Deere-specific shipment or margin conversion is supplied.
event_contributions.calculation: June evidence does not support a separately quantifiable incremental Q3 Deere GAAP earnings effect; EPS effect = $0.00/share.

event_contributions.affected_line: agricultural volume, mix, tariff cost, labor cost, and production absorption
event_contributions.transmission_path: Peer agricultural operating trends -> possible Deere PPA operating-profit read-through -> consolidated pretax income -> tax -> EPS.
assumptions: AGCO's GAAP earnings contain non-comparable items; CNH's cited metric is adjusted EBIT; Kubota's segment and accounting basis are not directly comparable.
The supplied comparable analysis concluded no defensible conversion from peer results into Deere GAAP net income and diluted EPS.
event_contributions.calculation: Comparable-only incremental EPS transfer coefficient = 0; EPS effect = $0.00/share.

earnings_bridge.calculation: Operating income = revenue x operating margin = $12,356m x 11.938% = $1,475.0m. Pretax income = $1,475.0m - $101.7m net non-operating expense + $0m pretax adjustments = $1,373.3m. Net income attributable to Deere = $1,373.3m x (1 - 25.0% tax rate) + $0m net-income adjustments = $1,030.0m. Diluted EPS = $1,030.0m / 270.5m diluted shares x 1 = $3.81 per share. This is consistent with the FY guidance midpoint bridge: FY $4,750m - reported H1 $2,429m = $2,321m implied H2, of which Q3 is $1,030m and Q4 is $1,291m.
assumptions: The $12,356m revenue input equals the absolute Q3 forecast for the linked requested Worldwide net sales and revenues metric.
The operating-margin input is a consolidated forecast calibration, not a reported segment margin.
The 25% tax rate is the midpoint of management's 24%-26% FY equipment-operations tax guidance and is used as the Q3 GAAP central case.
The bridge uses no discrete tax, noncontrolling-interest, impairment, settlement, or unquantified tariff adjustment.
The debt issuance in E4 is not assumed to raise net interest expense because the funding use is not disclosed; its illustrative gross impact is immaterial at displayed EPS precision.

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Q3 FY2026 PPA operating-profit forecast = $484m; projected change = $484m - prior reported Q2 FY2026 actual of $706m = -$222m. GUIDANCE bridge: FY2026 PPA sales = FY2025 PPA sales of $17,311m x (1 - 7.5% midpoint of the guided 5%-10% decline) = $16,013m. Less reported H1 PPA sales of $7,666m = $8,347m implied H2 sales. Q3 is 47.4% of H2, matching FY2025 PPA H2 revenue seasonality and retaining management's Q4-higher-than-Q3 company phasing: $8,347m x 47.4% = $3,956m. FY PPA operating profit = $16,013m x 12.0% midpoint margin = $1,922m; less H1 PPA operating profit of $845m = $1,077m implied H2. Q3 receives 45.0% of H2 profit because management expects the most favorable cost comparisons in Q4: $1,077m x 45.0% = $484m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA shipment volume, price, foreign-currency translation, material/freight/tariff production cost, and manufacturing absorption
event_contributions.transmission_path: PPA net sales decline and 11%-13% operating-margin outlook -> PPA revenue less COGS, R&D, SG&A, and other segment operating items -> PPA operating profit.
assumptions: FY2025 PPA net sales were $17,311m and FY2025 PPA operating margin was 15.4%.
The 5%-10% sales-decline range is represented by a 7.5% central case; the 11%-13% margin range is represented by a 12.0% central case.
Reported FY2026 H1 PPA sales were $7,666m and H1 PPA operating profit was $845m.
FY2025 PPA Q3 sales were $4,273m and implied Q4 sales were $4,740m, making Q3 47.4% of FY2025 PPA H2 sales.
Q3 receives only 45% of implied H2 PPA operating profit because management specifically indicated that cost comparisons improve most in Q4.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. FY PPA sales = $17,311m x (1 - 7.5%) = $16,013m. H2 sales = $16,013m - $7,666m reported H1 = $8,347m. Q3 sales = $8,347m x 47.4% = $3,956m. FY PPA operating profit = $16,013m x 12.0% = $1,922m. H2 operating profit = $1,922m - $845m = $1,077m. Q3 operating profit = $1,077m x 45.0% = $484m. Change versus prior Q2 actual = $484m - $706m = -$222m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA production cost / tariff cost
event_contributions.transmission_path: Reduced tariff rate on eligible imported agricultural equipment/components -> lower PPA COGS -> PPA operating profit.
assumptions: The event does not disclose Deere's eligible import values, whether affected goods are inputs or finished equipment, sourcing geography, or timing of customs entry.
Management's guidance already incorporates direct tariff costs and mitigation actions, so a gross policy change cannot be equated with a net incremental PPA COGS benefit.
event_contributions.calculation: MIXED ROUTE. The potential COGS benefit is conceptually positive but cannot be quantified or separated from tariff assumptions embedded in guidance; recognized Q3 PPA operating-profit contribution = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA retail demand, dealer inventories, shipment volume, and manufacturing absorption
event_contributions.transmission_path: May tractor/combine retail decline -> potential lower PPA dealer orders and shipments -> lower revenue and fixed-cost absorption -> PPA operating profit.
assumptions: AEM data are industry retail-sales data, not Deere shipments, and no Deere production response or PPA product-category sales base for May is disclosed.
Guidance already assumed weak North American large-ag demand, lower PPA shipment volumes, and production-cost headwinds.
E5 provides a more complete May-June demand signal and prevents assigning the May combine decline twice.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED READ-THROUGH. The May signal is negative but cannot be scaled to Deere PPA revenue or factory absorption after guidance; incremental Q3 PPA operating-profit contribution = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA operating expense and aftersales/service mix
event_contributions.transmission_path: Repair-resource compliance could affect PPA service support, software, administration, and dealer-service mix -> PPA other segment items -> PPA operating profit.
assumptions: No implementation cost, legal charge, revenue concession, or PPA allocation has been disclosed.
The stipulated order does not establish immediate Q3 accounting recognition.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. No quantified PPA operating-expense or margin effect is disclosed; incremental Q3 PPA operating-profit contribution = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: interest expense
event_contributions.transmission_path: Debt issuance affects consolidated/Financial Services interest expense and liquidity, not PPA segment operating profit, which is measured before external interest expense.
assumptions: PPA segment operating profit excludes the relevant external financing-cost effect.
No operating use-of-proceeds or PPA manufacturing investment effect is disclosed.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. PPA operating-profit contribution = $0m because the event is below the PPA segment operating-profit line.

event_contributions.affected_line: PPA retail demand, dealer inventories, shipment volume, and manufacturing absorption
event_contributions.transmission_path: June tractor decline and combine improvement -> dealer retail flow -> potential PPA shipments and production utilization -> PPA operating profit.
assumptions: The combined May-June data do not provide Deere's higher-horsepower, combine, regional, or dealer-inventory exposure weights.
The June combine gain and year-to-date category trends do not establish a deviation from management's guided PPA sales-decline and margin ranges.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED READ-THROUGH. The later June observation reduces the severity of the May combine signal; no incremental Q3 PPA operating-profit adjustment is defensible: $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: agricultural shipment volume, regional mix, price realization, tariff cost, labor cost, and production absorption
event_contributions.transmission_path: AGCO/CNH agricultural results -> industry context for Deere PPA volume and margin -> potential PPA operating profit.
assumptions: CNH's $93m adjusted-EBIT decline and 290-basis-point margin decline are not Deere GAAP PPA operating profit and cannot be transferred directly.
AGCO's regional signals and Kubota's blended Farm & Industrial Machinery segment lack Deere-equivalent PPA exposure and margin bases.
Comparable results overlap with the industry-demand risk already embedded in guidance and with E2/E5.
event_contributions.calculation: Comparable-only incremental transfer coefficient = 0. The peer evidence is directionally negative/mixed but does not support an exposure-adjusted Deere PPA USD operating-profit amount after avoiding double counting.
